summary: Sustained 429s for short chat requests after migrating subset of routes to weighted dedicated subpool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports sudden, sustained 429 responses for short (1–5 token) chat requests immediately after we migrated ~12 per-route endpoints to their dedicated weighted subpool. The bulk/batch jobs continue to succeed; user-facing interactive streams (low-latency) are returning 429s at a high rate.

Impact:
- ~30% of interactive chat calls fail with 429 during normal traffic windows for the last 6 hours.
- Affects BrightCart production site in us-east-1, causing UX degradation and support escalations.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool (tenant BrightCart), prod|us-east-1.
- Migration: per-route weight reassignment performed 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC via Console rollout job.
- Client SDKs: browser/websocket + server-side HTTP short requests.

Observed behavior:
- Short chat requests fail with 429s while concurrently-running batch tokenizer/embedding jobs proceed.
- 429s spike correlates with the time of the route-weight migration.

Expected behavior:
- Per-route weight migration should rebalance token windows without reducing short-request capacity below expected thresholds.

Workaround attempted by customer:
- Swapping affected routes back to shared pool (temporary) reduced 429s but not completely eliminated them.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Have a tenant with both long-running bulk jobs and low-latency chat routes.
2) Configure dedicated subpool and assign nonzero fractional weights to several interactive routes.
3) Trigger a route-weight migration via Console (canary -> full).
4) Observe 429s on low-latency endpoints while bulk requests continue.

Notes: Repro on our staging dedicated pool using small traffic generator reproduced 429s within 10 minutes.
logs:
Example 429 response headers from customer traces:
- x-rw-rate: 0/200
- x-rw-window: 60s
- x-rw-route-id: brc-chat-01
- request_id: rw-7a9b2

Edge/gateway sample lines (us-east-1):
[2026-03-10T02:18:03.122Z] gw-edge-12 rw.rate_reject route=brc-chat-01 tenant=brightcart tokens_requested=1 tokens_available=0 window_until=2026-03-10T02:17:20Z
[2026-03-10T02:18:03.123Z] gw-edge-12 forwarded to origin status=429 request_id=rw-7a9b2

Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/tenant-brightcart/rate-limiter-overview?orgId=1&from=1678450000000&to=1678452000000
investigation:
Initial findings:
- Correlation between migration event and immediate drop in per-route token bucket capacity for the affected routes.
- Token buckets for those routes show a sudden 'capacity shrink' by ~30% after migration.
- Bulk routes (batched jobs) were observed consuming expected tokens; accounting appears correct for large requests.
- Hypothesis: a rounding/scale bug in weight normalization during the reallocation step reduces per-route max_tokens for small-weight routes. When routes have small fractional weights, the allocator computes integer token window capacity with floor() leading to zero/minimal capacity for short requests.
- Another contributing factor: the refill scheduler uses a global epoch and a per-route 'credit_quota' computed as floor(global_window * normalized_weight) — this is sensitive to fixed-point math and to order of operations during migration.

Actions taken so far:
- Pulled detailed allocator logs from control plane for the migration window (ctl-logs-2026-03-10.tar.gz).
- Replayed migration in staging and recorded token-bucket sizes before/after.
- Reproduced symptom with synthetic traffic (replay id: replay-2026-03-10-01).
- Opened internal INT ticket for the allocator arithmetic review (INT-4520).
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Nair (Support): Acknowledged customer report; requested authorization to run staging repro. Asked BrightCart for traffic samples and exact Console steps.
2026-03-10 BrightCart (Customer): Provided Console export (routes.json) and sample logs. Confirmed rollback reduced but did not fully eliminate 429s.

2026-03-11 Ethan Brooks (SRE): Reproduced on staging; allocator logs show integer truncation in normalize_weights(). Filed PR to add ceil-based fallback to avoid zeroing small-weight routes. See PR https://github.com/redwood-infra/rate-limiter/pull/582.

2026-03-11 Priya Nair (Support): Notified customer of temporary mitigation: schedule migration in a low-traffic window and increment small route weights prior to migration. Will coordinate with Eng for patch rollout.

2026-03-12 BrightCart (Customer): Thank you — their traffic test showed improved success after we temporarily bumped small-route weights and replayed migration in staging. Awaiting permanent fix rollout.
2026-03-12 Ethan Brooks (SRE): Marking as In Progress; patch merged to main branch, queued for staged rollout (canary 2026-03-13 04:00 UTC). Postmortem runbook drafted at linked Confluence page.
resolution:
Workaround and permanent fix plan:
1) Short-term mitigation: For enterprise tenants performing route-weight migrations, recommend bumping any small fractional weights to a minimum threshold (e.g., 0.02) before migration. Re-run migration during low-traffic window.
2) Hotfix: PR 582 changes normalize_weights() to use ceil-based allocation with a minimum token floor for active routes; avoids zeroing small-weight interactive routes.
3) Rollout plan: Canary deploy to dedicated control plane 2026-03-13 04:00 UTC; monitor rate-limiter headroom metrics and customer 429 rate for 2 hours; progressive rollout to other regions if stable.
4) Follow-up: Postmortem and permanent guardrails to Console UI to warn when migrating routes with weights below threshold.

Customer notified of planned canary schedule and mitigation steps.
